title: POC: session ephemerality, anonymization & audit addendum (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This working draft captures a proposalset for a customer-facing POC around ephemeral session handling, minimal retention, and an accompanying DPA addendum that defines retention SLAs, auditability, and required controls. Target audience: solutions eng, SRE, and legal prepping a pilot with a regulated customer (fintech).

High-level goals (POC scope):
- Ensure session-level request/response data used for inference is treated as ephemeral by default (TTL <= 72 hours) unless explicitly opted-in.
- Provide cryptographically hashed identifiers for debugging that cannot be reversed without a customer-side secret.
- Preserve an auditable deletion and access trail for at-rest data and logs; surface deletion metrics to the customer via console & one-off reports.
- Offer a DPA addendum clause set that supports short retention windows, escrow for forensic requests, and clear subprocessors list.

Requirements (engineering / infra):
- Short-lived object stores: per-tenant session buckets with object lifecycle rules to auto-delete after configured TTL (default 72h).
- Metadata-only diagnostics: store only non-PHI metadata (latency, error codes, model id, coarse token counts) beyond TTL for 90 days; raw inputs/outputs tossed at TTL.
- Ephemeral cache segregation: KV caches used for inference must be ephemeral and cleared on session termination; no persistent dumps.
- Re-identification mitigation: PII detection pipeline before any persistence; if PII detected, auto-redact/pseudonymize per policy.
- Crypto hashing: use HKDF with customer-supplied salt (where available) for any stable identifier we must preserve for troubleshooting.
- Audit pipeline: append-only access log (who/what/why) written to encrypted long-term archive for 365 days, with index only (no raw payload).

Operational SLAs and metrics (POC targets):
- Deletion completion: 99.9% of TTL-expiry deletes must complete within 15 minutes of lifecycle trigger.
- Manual deletion request (API): 95% completed within 6 hours, 99.9% within 72 hours.
- Deletion verification: daily job that samples and verifies purge for each tenant.
- Retained-by-error incidents: target < 1 per 10k deletion ops; incidents trigger automated paging and customer notice.

DPA addendum: proposed language snippets (draft):
1) Data retention and deletion
"Customer Data used for inference (including inputs, outputs, intermediate representations) shall be treated as ephemeral by default. Provider shall delete such Customer Data no later than seventy-two (72) hours after collection, unless Customer explicitly requests longer retention via documented opt-in. Where Customer requests retention for debugging, stored data shall be isolated in a customer-scoped bucket marked for retention and access-limited to named Redwood personnel and the Customer's administrators."

2) Auditability and access logs
"Provider will maintain an immutable access log recording access to Customer Data, including the identity of the accessor, purpose, and timestamp. Audit logs will not contain raw Customer Data. Audit logs shall be retained for a period of one (1) year and can be exported on request for compliance review subject to redaction rules."

3) Pseudonymization and key controls
"Where stable identifiers are required to correlate events, Provider shall store only pseudonymized identifiers derived via a one-way keyed hash function. The key material for reversible diagnostics (if any) will be customer-managed where possible; Provider-held keys (if used) will be stored in an HSM and rotated every 90 days."

4) Forensic escrow and lawful requests
"Provider will support a forensic escrow mechanism for court-ordered or regulatory requests: encrypted snapshots may be escrowed for a customer-defined period subject to mutual approval. Provider will notify Customer of lawful data requests to the extent permitted by law and will cooperate in narrow, scoped disclosures only."

5) Subprocessors and cross-border transfer
"Provider shall provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors and will notify Customer of any changes with 30 days' notice. Cross-border transfer of Customer Data is limited to jurisdictions agreed in writing; otherwise, Provider will employ standard contractual clauses or equivalent measures."

Implementation notes (engineering specifics):
- Lifecycle enforcement: use cloud-native lifecycle rules + an idempotent deletion worker with queue backpressure handling. Worker must emit deletion success/failure events to the audit pipeline.
- Deletion verification: add a verification lambda that compares object listing vs. expected TTL tombstone list nightly.
- Redaction pipeline: integrate a lightweight PII classifier at ingress (open-source or 3rd-party) and a deterministic redactor for common entities (SSNs, emails, account numbers). Flag uncertain cases for manual review (rare).
- Metrics surface: add console pulse showing TTL config, last purge time, deletion success rate, and manual delete requests pending. Include an exportable CSV for auditors.
- Opt-in retention UX: product needs an explicit checkbox + retention justification field + admin audit trail. No default opt-in.

Customer-facing controls and choices (POC options):
- Default ephemeral (72h) with metadata retention 90d.
- Extended retention (30d / 90d / custom) via signed SOW or console approval with explicit justification.
- Customer-managed salt for stable pseudonyms vs. Provider-managed HSM key (tradeoff: security vs. ease of support).
- Forensic escrow: on-demand or periodic snapshots (chargeable).

Open items / legal questions to resolve:
- Is 72h default acceptable to the customer/legal team, or do they require 24h or <24h for specific regulated flows?
- Acceptance criteria for redaction failures (false negatives): what is allowable risk threshold?
- SLA language for deletion completion windows — align legal wording to metrics above.
- Whether audit logs containing indexed pointers (object ids, non-PII) are permissible to share with auditors or must be redacted.

Next steps / action items:
- Solutions eng: build a short demo showing auto-delete lifecycle + deletion verification job (owner: Aisha) — target prototype by 2025-12-10.
- SRE: define deletion worker scaling and error dashboard (owner: Ravi) — design doc due 2025-12-05.
- Legal: review DPA snippet and prepare a customer-ready addendum template (owner: Samir) — initial review by 2025-11-25.
- Product: scope UX for opt-in retention and admin approvals (owner: Elena) — wireframes by 2025-12-01.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting playbook (for POC)
- If a customer reports data not deleted after TTL: check deletion worker queue and error logs; run manual purge (documented) and notify customer within 4 hours.
- If redaction pipeline flags high uncertain rate (>5% of sessions): pause retention opt-ins and escalate to ML team to tune classifier.
- If audit log export requested: produce index-only export first; escalate redaction/legal review for any containing potential identifiers.

Notes / rationale (brief):
- Default ephemeral with opt-in balances developer UX (debugging) and risk posture for regulated customers.
- Separation of raw payloads from audit indexes lets us prove access without retaining sensitive content.
- Customer-managed salts/keys substantially reduce re-identification risk and are recommended for high-regulation pilots.

End of draft.

Document history:
- 2025-11-12: initial notes and scoping (Aisha)
- 2025-11-20: added SLA targets and draft DPA language after sync with Legal (Samir)
- 2025-12-02: revised implementation notes after SRE review (Ravi)
